messages:
alex: hey team — running terraform plan in staging after importing a helm release and it just hangs during provider refresh. sometimes I see a state lock appear and then the plan never progresses. anyone run into this before? :thinking:

maya: can you paste the last ~20 lines of the plan output and the exact error? also which terraform & helm provider versions?

alex: here's what I'm seeing when it stalls:
```
$ terraform plan -var-file=staging.tfvars
Refreshing Terraform state in-memory prior to plan...

Error: Error refreshing state: Error when reading resource "helm_release.app": 404 Not Found: release not found

# then it just blocks trying to reach the cluster and the state lock shows up in dynamodb
```

joel: couple quick checks — is that release actually in the cluster? and did you import a release id that doesn't match the helm provider's expected id format? also check the remote lock table (dynamo) for the lock owner. if previous apply crashed you might need to force-unlock.

alex: release is present in cluster. I imported with `terraform import helm_release.app my-app-2026-03-15` (that was the release name). tried `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` once, lock cleared, but plan re-acquires lock and stalls during refresh again.

sam: could be kubeconfig/session expiry — refresh will call into k8s/helm and hang if auth loops. can you run `kubectl get secret -n myns` from the TF agent host to confirm cluster access? also check the helm provider config (tiller vs helm3 differences).

alex: kubectl works fine from my machine. interestingly the helm_release resource in state has an id like `my-app.v1` while the actual release name is `my-app-2026-03-15`. maybe the import created a mismatch.

tara: if the state id doesn't match what the provider expects, refresh will try to look up the wrong release and hang. options: 1) backup state, `terraform state rm helm_release.app` and re-import with the exact id the provider expects, or 2) use `terraform refresh -target=helm_release.app` to isolate, or 3) plan with `-refresh=false` to at least get an apply plan you can review. i'd do a state backup first. :warning:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: plan requested by alex on staging (run id: r-3061234). Status: queued.

maya: also check provider version — there was a change in id format in helm provider v2.4.0 (it switched to using `name.namespace` vs `name` in some configs). if you imported with an older provider, the id might be different.

alex: good catch — provider.tf has helm provider pinned to ~> 2.3. I'm going to try: 1) backup state; 2) `terraform state rm helm_release.app`; 3) re-import using the id the provider expects (`my-app.myns`), then run `terraform plan -target=helm_release.app`. i'll report back.

sam: if you want to unblock a canary deploy quickly, run `terraform plan -refresh=false -target=module.api` then apply that module only. it'll skip refresh but still produce diffs for the target. not ideal long-term but useful for fast rollback.

alex: trying the import fix now. thanks all. i'll ping here when done. :raised_hands:

maya: one more: when you re-import, run `terraform state show helm_release.app` and validate the `id` field matches `kubectl get secrets -n myns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'` patterns so we don't mismatch again.

alex: update — reimported with `terraform import helm_release.app my-app.myns` and plan completed after that. looks like the id mismatch was the root cause. leaving the lock alone for now but will monitor. thanks for the pointers. :ok_hand:

joel: nice. if it happens again, also check for duplicate runs from CI that can re-acquire locks (race).

alex: noted. closing this thread unless anyone wants a postmortem doc.

maya: :thumbsup:
